guard: every harness renders the same briefing paragraphs from one module, each adds only the sentence that says how a peer message arrives, and the gateway leaves that sentence out
why: Six connectors used to assemble their own briefing from the shared sentences, and the copies
drifted: Codex and Jcode carried a shorter reply etiquette, OpenCode and Hermes carried no
feedback or etiquette paragraph, pi carried no orientation or channel guidance. The module
composes the paragraphs once; the cells grade that composition, not any connector's copy.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports by RELATIVE SOURCE PATH
(../src/index.js), so the bytes mutated are the bytes graded. No dist is in the path and no
M1 is the drift that shipped: a connector that forgets one paragraph. M2 is the gateway's
exception going the other way, an arrival sentence that would contradict the connect result's
own listening line. M3 is the identity line losing the role, which the orientation card and
every harness used to agree on.

mutations.name: M1 drop the reply etiquette paragraph
mutations.expectRed: every harness carries the reply etiquette
mutations.cell: every harness carries the reply etiquette
mutations.note: The paragraph Codex and Jcode carried only in a shorter copy, and OpenCode and Hermes not at all.

mutations.name: M2 give the gateway an arrival sentence of its own
mutations.replace: gateway: "Peer messages are delivered into your turns as blocks marked 📨.",
mutations.expectRed: the gateway briefing leaves the arrival sentence out
mutations.cell: the gateway briefing leaves the arrival sentence out
mutations.note: A gateway conversation hears messages however its embedder says in the connect result; a sentence here would contradict it.

mutations.name: M3 drop the role from the identity line
mutations.expectRed: every harness opens with the identity line
mutations.cell: every harness opens with the identity line
mutations.note: The role is what cotal_anycast routes on; a seat not told its role does not know which requests are its own.
